why: The ferry's teleport taken off its repeatable tiller and hung on the far beat's own completion bundle instead. A teleport fired by an objective's completion is a gather: it carries whoever is in the deck's box once, and a party of four boarding one at a time leaves three on the deck, so the route proof does not lean on it and the leg from the deck to the cabin has no way. The graph's `carry` edge is restated as a `walk` in the same edit, because a carry no link realises is refused at validation (DW0934) before the build reaches the walk; as a walk, the graph claims what the author of this probe claims, and the geometry answers it. It declares no unit: the teleport and the trigger are surfaces the primary binds. The refusal names the teleport, says it fires from a root the party cannot fire again, and prescribes the primary's own shape — a `use` trigger declared `once: false` hosting the same effect — with no doorway, gap or fence in it, because a walk was never the way.
